title: St. Jude Health - On-prem Air-gapped Discovery
summary: Discovery call for St. Jude Health to evaluate Redwood Private in an air-gapped, on-prem environment. Focus on offline updates, hardware constraints, security controls (KMS/HSM, SSO, audit logs), and pilot scope. Team requested security pack, hardware checklist, and an on-site/hybrid pilot plan.
next_steps: Aisha to send SOC 2/ISO docs and security pack
Devon to schedule technical deep-dive and provide bench test checklist
Kevin to share current infra inventory and preferred hardware list
Schedule 2-week pilot window and arrange physical media workflow review
action_items: Aisha Patel — Send SOC 2, ISO27001 doc, and Redwood Private security pack — due 2025-12-20
Devon Chen — Prepare bench script and sample prompt set for throughput/latency tests — due 2025-12-22
Kevin Lin — Share rack specs, GPU models, and air-gap change control process — due 2025-12-19
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 min
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Devon Chen (Redwood SE), Lara Kim (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (CISO, St. Jude), Dr. Alan Price (Head of AI), Kevin Lin (Infra Lead), Priya Rao (Compliance)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand St. Jude's on-prem air-gapped requirements and feasibility for Redwood Private. Discussed offline update workflows, hardware, KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO, and pilot next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'll kick us off. quick intros, then we'll dive into your constraints.
00:15 Speaker 2 (Maria): hi, maria here, ciso. we're evaluating options for hosting models on prem because of patient data regs. main concerns are air gap, patching updates and key mgmt.
00:30 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): alan here. our team wants to run clinical note summarization and a couple of retrievers, and we need predictable latency for triage flows. also the model weight size matters for our hardware.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Aisha): great. Devon, do you want to add a bit on how Redwood Private works and common patterns?
00:50 Speaker 4 (Devon): yeah sure. so Redwood Private is basically our private control plane plus a customer-managed runtime deployed inside your network. for air-gapped we support an offline install path — we can ship a signed bundle that your infra team imports via physical media, it includes the runtime, model artifacts, and our operators. there are a few patterns: fully isolated with manual updates, or hybrid with a control-plane proxy for meta updates.
01:12 Speaker 5 (Kevin): sorry can I interrupt — when you say model artifacts, is that whole weights? and how large are we talking? we run H100s and a few A100s in different racks, some older nodes.
01:30 Speaker 4 (Devon): good question. yes, we can deliver model weights. sizes vary by model and quantization. for example a 7B FP16 might be tens of gig, 70B can be 100s of gigs, but with quantization to int8 or q4_0 we can dramatically reduce disk. for H100 we generally see better perf but we support A100 as well. for air-gapped installs we provide a compressed signed package and checksums.
01:58 Speaker 2 (Maria): what about key management? we can't have keys leaving the VPC or any cloud KMS.
02:05 Speaker 4 (Devon): understood. we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. for air-gapped sites we support on-prem HSMs and customer-managed key material; Redwood doesn't hold the private keys. the bundle can be encrypted and keys are injected locally. there is also support for bring-your-own-KMS integrations — we'll work with your security team on the key workflow.
02:30 Speaker 5 (Kevin): and updates — we have a change-control board, no inbound connections allowed. what's the update cadence and can we do hot patches?
02:40 Speaker 4 (Devon): typically customers plan periodic update windows. For security fixes we provide patches that you can apply offline; the runtime supports safe upgrade paths with rollback. hot patching in an air-gapped environment is manual — we'll provide a validation checklist and can remote into the environment via a scheduled, pre-approved bastion if you want a hybrid option.
03:10 Speaker 6 (Priya): our compliance team will need audit logs, who accessed what models and prompts (at least meta), and retention policies. do you capture that in Redwood Private?
03:18 Speaker 4 (Devon): yes, Redwood Private includes local audit logs and can export to your SIEM. logs are configurable for retention and masked fields; we can ship preconfigured dashboards in the console, but in air-gapped mode dashboards run locally.
03:30 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): latency — we're sensitive. can we run a bench with our workload? and are there auto-scaling options on prem?
03:45 Speaker 4 (Devon): absolutely. we typically run a bench script with your prompt set — measure p50/p95 token latency and throughput. autoscaling on prem depends on your infra — we support node-level autoscaling hooks and a policy engine, but in strictly air-gapped racks it's often manual or based on Kubernetes cluster autoscaler if you have that.
04:05 Speaker 1 (Aisha): just to capture business context — what's your timeline and success criteria for this project?
04:12 Speaker 5 (Kevin): timeline is Q1 pilot, production in Q2 if the pilot goes well. success criteria are: pass security review, latency under 300ms p50 for the summarization flow, and stable throughput for nightly batch jobs.
04:30 Speaker 2 (Maria): and also we need to confirm we can comply with our data residency rules and that the model updates won't leak telemetry.
04:40 Speaker 4 (Devon): we can disable outbound telemetry entirely in Private and air-gapped modes — nothing leaves unless you opt in.
04:48 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): one more technical — how do you handle KV cache persistence across restarts and is it secure in air-gapped mode? we've had issues with cold-start costs before.
04:58 Speaker 4 (Devon): KV cache can be persisted locally and encrypted at rest with your KMS. We also support warm pools to reduce cold starts; details depend on model and sequence lengths.
05:15 Speaker 6 (Priya): what about attestations and compliance artifacts — do you have a package we can share with auditors?
05:20 Speaker 1 (Aisha): yes, we have a security pack — SOC2, ISO certs, architecture diagrams, data flow, and an on-prem runbook. I'll send that after this call.
05:30 Speaker 5 (Kevin): license model — how does pricing work for Private on-prem? is there a perpetual license or subscription?
05:36 Speaker 1 (Aisha): typically enterprise licensing — platform fee plus support tier, sometimes with committed capacity for Dedicated but for Private it's often an annual license plus support; we can share options and a draft commercial.
05:48 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): curious about model governance — if we want to pin a model version or fallback to a smaller model during load, is that supported?
05:55 Speaker 4 (Devon): yes, model pinning and automatic fallback policies are supported; we can configure routes by latency or cost and set automatic downgrade to a compatible variant if your preferred model isn't available.
06:10 Speaker 2 (Maria): supply chain security — how do we validate the signed bundles? do you provide SBOMs for the runtime and kernel modules?
06:20 Speaker 4 (Devon): we provide signed artifacts, checksums, and SBOMs. for kernel-level modules or custom runtime libs we supply hashes and signatures; your security team can validate them during the import process.
06:35 Speaker 5 (Kevin): hardware note — some of our racks are older and don't have NVLink across the full chassis. will that affect model serving?
06:42 Speaker 4 (Devon): it can. interconnect impacts large-model sharding and latency. for very large models we recommend H100 with NVLink or local model parallel strategies. For fragmented racks we can recommend quantized model flavors or smaller-sized models.
07:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): do you have any preferred model sizes to start with for the pilot?
07:05 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): 7B or 13B would be fine for the initial pilot if we can meet latency. we may evaluate a 70B for more complex reasoning later.
07:12 Speaker 4 (Devon): good plan. we'll propose a bench with 13B quantized and a 70B small sample to show degradation curve.
07:25 Speaker 6 (Priya): legal — if we go air-gapped, will Redwood still have any ability to access logs or data? we need contractual guarantees.
07:35 Speaker 1 (Aisha): in Private air-gapped deployments we don't retain your data; contractual language can specify no telemetry retention and strict SLAs about access. we'll loop in legal.
07:48 Speaker 5 (Kevin): patching cadence — are there emergency security fixes and what's the process to approve and apply them?
07:55 Speaker 4 (Devon): emergency fixes are delivered as signed hotfix bundles. your change board will need to approve the import; we provide a pre-check script and rollback steps. we can also provide a test harness to run in a staging rack before production.
08:15 Speaker 2 (Maria): backups — what's the backup strategy for model artifacts and KV caches?
08:22 Speaker 4 (Devon): backups are customer-managed; we recommend encrypted snapshots to an internal artifact store. for large models we use delta replication for patches to save bandwidth during offline updates.
08:40 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): on the bench — do you measure token cost or is that more of a hosted metric? we want to estimate TCO per request.
08:50 Speaker 4 (Devon): we can provide unit economics based on throughput and GPU hours for the model and quantization profile. the bench will produce per-token latency and estimated GPU-hours for your workload.
09:05 Speaker 1 (Aisha): ok let's move into a couple of clarifying questions from our side about your environment. Kevin, do you have an inventory doc you can share?
09:12 Speaker 5 (Kevin): yes I'll export the rack-by-rack and share. note some nodes are on older CentOS images.
09:20 Speaker 4 (Devon): that's fine, we support mainstream kernels but we'll need to validate driver versions, CUDA and NCCL. we provide a compatibility matrix.
09:30 Speaker 6 (Priya): do you support SSO/SAML? we need role-based access control.
09:36 Speaker 4 (Devon): yes, SSO with SAML is supported, RBAC is configurable and can map to your existing IdP groups. in air-gapped mode SAML metadata can be exchanged offline.
09:50 Speaker 2 (Maria): one more — how do you handle model licensing for third-party models? are there restrictions if we bring custom models?
09:58 Speaker 4 (Devon): for BYO models you manage licensing; Redwood will not redistribute. we can help with packaging and ensuring compatibility for runtime. for third-party models that have special license terms we surface that in the onboarding checklist.
10:15 Speaker 1 (Aisha): good. any blockers from the compliance side? Priya?
10:20 Speaker 6 (Priya): just need the security pack and confirmation about no telemetry, plus the SBOMs. also want to see evidence of past air-gapped deployments.
10:30 Speaker 1 (Aisha): we have references — we'll include a short case study and contact.
10:35 Speaker 5 (Kevin): another ops concern — we sometimes power-cycle racks during maintenance, how tolerant is the runtime to sudden node loss?
10:42 Speaker 4 (Devon): runtime is designed for graceful degradation; for critical traffic we recommend multi-rack redundancy and model replicas. KV cache persistence plus warm pools will reduce impact.
10:55 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): can you talk briefly about quantization support and accuracy tradeoffs? we've seen hallucination increase with heavy quantization.
11:05 Speaker 4 (Devon): yeah so quantization reduces memory but can change float behavior. we provide recommended quantization profiles per model and test suites that compare output quality. if quality matters, we can run an eval set to measure regression and tune the quant profile.
11:30 Speaker 1 (Aisha): ok let's capture next steps. we'll send the security pack, a bench script, and a suggested pilot plan. any other asks?
11:40 Speaker 5 (Kevin): include a simple physical-media import runbook — step-by-step for our change board.
11:48 Speaker 6 (Priya): please include an expected timeline for each deliverable.
11:55 Speaker 2 (Maria): also include SLA options for Private — e.g., response times for P1.
12:05 Speaker 1 (Aisha): noted. we'll send those items and then schedule a technical deep dive next week. thanks everyone.
12:15 Speaker 3 (Dr. Price): thanks, appreciate it.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, "hotfix" sometimes transcribed as "hot fix"). References: security pack link (sent post-call), bench script (to be provided), import runbook (to be provided).
